title: Defend an Agentic-AI Classification
summary: Produce a human-reviewed evidence dossier that classifies an exact system without hiding uncertainty or overstating autonomy.
objectives: Classify a version-scoped experience across all eight taxonomy classes.
Support every material claim with documented, tested, inferred, or unknown evidence.
Compare deterministic, single-agent, and multi-agent alternatives using equivalent cases.
Earn mastery through knowledge score, critical gates, artifacts, and human review.

sections.title: Freeze the unit of classification
paragraphs: Record the product surface, versions, configuration, model, tools, permissions, state services, runtime, observation date, and accountable owner. Exclude behavior you did not observe or cannot source.
State the question precisely. A useful dossier answers what this configured experience did and who controlled it, not whether an entire brand is intelligent, autonomous, or agentic.

sections.title: Build the claim and behavior ledger
paragraphs: For each classification signal, attach a first-party source or retained run artifact. Keep documented and tested evidence separate, identify inferences, and preserve unknowns with a resolution plan.

Trace next-step selection, tools, external effects, state, feedback, coordination, stop conditions, recovery, and human authority. A missing critical boundary prevents a confident agentic classification.

sections.title: Compare the least complex alternatives
paragraphs: Use equivalent cases to compare a deterministic workflow, bounded single-agent design, and multi-agent design where applicable. Measure outcome quality, safety, latency, cost, coordination overhead, recovery, trajectory, and review load.
Do not reward autonomy or agent count. Select the least complex design that passes critical gates and meets the declared need.

sections.title: Make uncertainty and authority visible
paragraphs: The final disposition states the classification, supporting evidence, rejected alternatives, residual unknowns, expiry date, and triggers for re-review.
A qualified person reviews the evidence and critical errors. The system or model being classified cannot approve its own mastery or publication.

activity.title: Create and defend the classification dossier
instructions: Freeze one exact experience and create its layer, control-flow, and responsibility maps.
Build a dated claim ledger with documented, tested, inference, and unknown labels.
Compare equivalent deterministic, single-agent, and multi-agent designs when the evidence supports them.
Submit the classification, residual uncertainty, review date, and human disposition for challenge and revision.
evidence: Four required dossier artifacts with traceable claims and no critical classification errors.
A recorded human review that accepts, rejects, or returns the dossier with corrective evidence.
activity.reflectionPrompt: What evidence would most likely cause you to change this classification?

cues.text: Freeze the system boundary before accepting any classification claim.
Show the dossier linking scope, behavior signals, claim evidence, unknowns, comparison, and disposition.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: A hierarchical text outline connects each classification claim to its evidence, boundary, uncertainty, review date, and human disposition. Reduced-motion mode shows the complete outline.

cues.text: Build a claim ledger that preserves sources, run evidence, inference, and unknowns.
Compare equivalent deterministic, single-agent, and multi-agent cases without rewarding complexity.
Record residual uncertainty, expiry, and accountable human disposition.
Check whether every critical error is absent before scoring the dossier.
Guide dossier assembly, peer challenge, correction, and submission.
Begin the check only after every required artifact is ready for human review.

capstone.title: Agentic-AI Classification Dossier
capstone.summary: Classify one exact product experience and defend the result with current sources, run evidence, comparative design evidence, unknowns, and human review.

criteria.title: Exact scope and taxonomy
criteria.description: The dossier names the exact experience and applies the eight-class taxonomy without provider generalization or marketing-label shortcuts.

criteria.title: Control and responsibility boundaries
criteria.description: Next-step control, tools, effects, state, feedback, coordination, stopping, recovery, and human authority are accurately located.

criteria.title: Evidence quality and freshness
criteria.description: Claims use current primary sources and retained tests while documentation, testing, inference, and unknowns remain distinct.

criteria.title: Equivalent design comparison
criteria.description: The learner compares appropriate deterministic, single-agent, and multi-agent alternatives on equivalent cases and rejects unnecessary complexity.

criteria.title: Critical classification safety
criteria.description: The dossier contains no tool-call-equals-agent, model-harness collapse, hidden unknown, missing authority, or unsupported autonomy error.

criteria.title: Human disposition
criteria.description: An accountable reviewer records the decision, residual uncertainty, expiry, and re-review triggers without delegating approval to a model.

questions.prompt: What must a classification dossier freeze first?
choices: The exact product surface, version, configuration, tools, permissions, and observation date
questions.explanation: A defensible classification begins with a precise unit and operating context.

questions.prompt: Which evidence combination supports an agentic-system classification?
choices: A bounded goal-directed loop plus tool, state, feedback, control, recovery, and authority evidence
questions.explanation: The complete system boundary must be observable and evidenced.

questions.prompt: When should a multi-agent design be selected?
choices: When equivalent evidence shows separate agents and coordination add necessary value
When it produces the longest trace
questions.explanation: Multi-agent complexity must be justified by measured need and explicit coordination.

questions.prompt: Can a score above 80 percent override a critical classification error?
choices: No; critical gates must also pass
questions.explanation: Knowledge score is necessary but critical errors and applied evidence remain blocking.

questions.prompt: Who approves the final applied mastery disposition?
questions.explanation: Human review retains authority over applied mastery and publication.
